messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SEV2 - model-inference-high-latency triggered for service=redwood-runtime region=us-west-2
incident-bot: metric: p95_latency_ms > 450ms for 3/3 intervals · Pager: @alex · Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inference-latency
alex: seeing it. p95 jumped to ~620ms about 2m ago. traffic spike to a specific model variant?
priya: confirming increased tail latency, looks correlated with batch sizes ~1. Queue depth spiked on gpu-node-17.
alex: Im pulling runtime logs and tailing the scheduler. can someone check autoscale events? @marta?
marta: checking autoscaler now. no scale-up events in the last 10m. reserved pool seems saturated.
priya: logs show continuous batching backlog + a couple of requests stuck at KV-cache warmup.
alex: ok mitigation: will temporarily increase max replicas for dedicated-pool-2 and reduce batching window from 20ms -> 5ms to prioritize latency. doing change now.
opsbot: Change applied: deployment/dedicated-pool-2 replicas scaled from 8 -> 12 (user: alex).
priya: after scale: p95 down to ~380ms, p99 still ~820ms. progress but still noisy pages possible.
marta: agree. we should avoid more wakeups to oncall. suggest we tune alert routing: keep sev2 for global outage only, move sustained tail-latency-only alerts to ticket (sev3) and route to eng-sre channel.
alex: +1. this thread agrees? we need to make a fast config change and follow up with a post-incident evaluation for thresholds and dashboards.
priya: I can push an interim alert change: alert rule will require p99>1000ms for 2 intervals to page, p95>500ms -> ticket. Doable in alert manager now.
marta: also we should add a dashboard tile for model-variant breakdown (by model_id + quantization profile) — current dashboards aggregate across variants and hide the hot-spot.
alex: please add a short note in incident channel: who is doing what. Priya, you change alert; Marta, you create dashboard and a muted alert route; I'll draft the PagerDuty escalation rule change doc and open the follow-up ticket.
priya: changing rule now. patch:
```yaml
alert: ModelInferenceHighLatency
expr: max_over_time(redwood_runtime_latency_p99[2m]) > 1000
for: 2m
severity: page
route: pager-duty
---
alert: ModelInferenceHighLatency_p95
expr: max_over_time(redwood_runtime_latency_p95[5m]) > 500
for: 3m
severity: ticket
route: eng-sre
```
priya: pushed to AlertManager as interim. will monitor for 10m then we can revert or adjust.
opsbot: AlertManager: config reload succeeded (user: priya).
alex: good. reduce noise now. everyone, please add quick notes to the runbook about this interim threshold so next oncall sees it.
marta: creating dashboard card + adding variant breakdown. putting a temp pin on node-17 metrics to watch.
priya: monitoring: p95 holding ~340ms, p99 ~760ms and trending down. paging suppressed per new rule.
alex: taking a 15m watch. @sam will take the 02:00 handoff — Sam, FYI: increased replicas on dedicated-pool-2, interim AlertManager rules (p99 page threshold 1000ms), follow-ups: RED-4321 (alert routing + severity review), RED-4322 (dashboard variant breakdown), update runbook.
sam: ack, will take over at handoff. please document the exact AlertManager commit hash in the ticket.
priya: noted. commit: a1b9c3f (interim latency routing) added to RED-4321.
marta: assigning dashboard task to myself and priya for eval. will include a comparison view and suggested thresholds.
alex: ok team — before we close this thread: decision summary to include in post-incident notes: 1) temporary pages suppressed by raising p99 threshold -> reduces noisy wakeups, 2) move p95 alerts to ticket to reduce paging for small transient degradations, 3) add per-variant dashboard + runbook steps for KV-cache warmup.
priya: filing the post-incident Jira: RED-4321 created, link: https://jira.redwood/browse/RED-4321. tagging eng-sre and devex for follow-up.
incident-bot: Incident update: SEV2 -> mitigated state at 1769002720. Duration: ~25m. Pager duty escalation paused.
alex: thanks everyone. follow-ups assigned. leaving the channel to rest.
sam: taking over watch, will alert if anything drifts. good job. :thumbsup:
